'''Germar Rudolf''' (born 29 October 1964), also known as '''Germar Scheerer''',<ref name="Mentel2009">{{cite book |last1=Mentel |first1=Christian |title=Rudolf, Germar. In Benz, Wolfgang, ed. Handbuch Des Antisemitismus Judenfeindschaft in Geschichte Und Gegenwart. Band 2, Personen |date=2009 |publisher=De Gruyter Saur |isbn=9783598441592 |pages=701–702}}</ref><ref name="Long2002">{{cite journal |last1=Long |first1=Anthony |title=Forgetting the Führer: the recent history of the Holocaust denial movement in Germany |journal=Australian Journal of Politics and History |date=2002 |volume=48 |issue=1 |pages=72–84 |doi=10.1111/1467-8497.00253 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1467-8497.00253|url-access=subscription }}</ref> is a German chemist and a convicted [[Holocaust denial|Holocaust denier]].<ref>"A German court sentenced Holocaust denier Germar Rudolf to two and a half years in prison for [[incitement to ethnic or racial hatred|inciting racial hatred]] in publications and Web sites which "systematically" called into question the Nazi genocide." [http://www.dw-world.de/dw/article/0,2144,2386563,00.html "German Holocaust Denier Imprisoned for Inciting Racial Hatred"], ''[[Deutsche Welle]]'', 16 February 2007.</ref>

==Background==
Rudolf was born in [[Limburg an der Lahn]], [[Hesse]]. In 1983 he took his [[Abitur]] in [[Remscheid]], then studied chemistry in [[Bonn]], graduating in 1989 with a master's degree.<ref name="Atkins2009"/> As a student, he joined the ''A.V. Tuisconia Königsberg zu Bonn'' and the ''K.D.St.V. Nordgau Prag zu Stuttgart'', [[Catholic]] [[Studentenverbindung|fraternities]] belonging to the [[Cartellverband]]. According to the website “[[Informationsdienst gegen Rechtsextremismus]]” (Information service against right-wing extremism), Rudolf was in 1985, a member of Schlesische Jugend (Silesian Youth), the youth section of the association The [[Landsmannschaft Schlesien|Landsmannschaft Schlesien - Nieder- und Oberschlesien e.V.]] ("Territorial Association of Silesia - Lower and Upper Silesia").<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=IDGR - Informationsdienst gegen Rechtsextremismus |title=Germar Rudolf - Biography |url=https://phdn.org/negation/rudolf/idgrrudolf.html }}</ref> Still according to the site Informationsdienst gegen Rechtsextremismus, Rudolf participated the year after, at the Reichsgründungskommers (Reich Foundation Parties) of the ultra-nationalist student association [[Verein Deutscher Studenten|Verein deutscher Studenten]] (VDSt, German Student League).<ref name=":0" /> In 1989, he also took on editorial responsibilities in the German newspaper of New Right ''[[Junge Freiheit]]'', and was an author in the far-right journals: ''Staatsbriefe'', ''Sleipnir'', ''Deutschland in Geschichte und Gegenwart.''<ref name="science">{{cite news |last=Green |first=Richard J |title=Chemistry is Not the Science: Rudolf, Rhetoric, and Reduction |url=http://www.holocaust-history.org/auschwitz/chemistry/not-the-science/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080604152626/http://www.holocaust-history.org/auschwitz/chemistry/not-the-science/ |archive-date=4 June 2008 |access-date=26 May 2008}}</ref> After supporting the [[Christian Social Union of Bavaria|CSU]]/[[Christian Democratic Union (Germany)|CDU]], he became a member of the [[Republicans (Germany)|Republicans]], a minor anti-immigrant German political party.<ref name="Mentel2009"/> After his military service with the [[German Air Force]], in October 1990 he joined the [[Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research]] at [[Stuttgart]], where he prepared a [[PhD]] thesis.<ref name="Grumke2002">{{cite book |editor1=Grumke, Thomas |editor2= Wagner, Bernd |title=Handbuch Rechtsradikalismus |date=2002 |publisher=Leske und Budrich |location=Opladen |isbn=978-3-8100-3399-4 |pages=133, 312–314}}</ref>

==The Rudolf Report==
In 1991, Rudolf began work on a paper entitled ''Report on the formation and verifiability of cyanide compounds in the Auschwitz "gas chambers"'' on behalf of the attorney of [[Otto Ernst Remer]], a former ''[[Wehrmacht]]'' general charged with ''[[Volksverhetzung]]'' (inciting hatred).  In 1993, this work was reported in the media. Rudolf was dismissed when his superiors discovered that he had used stationery from the Max Planck institute to commission the Institute Fresenius to analyze his samples from Auschwitz; the Max Planck Institute asserted that the use of its notepaper to make the request had mislead the testing laboratory into believing Rudolf's work was being done on its behalf.  Rudolf sued the Institute for wrongful dismissal; the lawsuit was settled without any monetary compensation, but with an agreement that his dismissal would be treated as a termination by mutual agreement.<ref name="Nature1994">{{cite journal |last1=Abbot |first1=Allison |title=Holocaust denial research disclaimed |journal=Nature |date=1994 |volume=368 |issue=6471 |page=483 |doi=10.1038/368483a0 |bibcode=1994Natur.368..483A |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/368483a0.pdf}}</ref> In 1996, the [[University of Stuttgart]] asked Rudolf to withdraw his application for a final PhD examination, or it would be denied, rendering his PhD thesis worthless. The legal basis for this is a German law which allows universities to deny or withdraw academic degrees where the candidate has used his academic credentials or knowledge to commit a crime. Rudolf has no Ph.D.<ref name="Pall">{{cite book |last1=Pelt |first1=Robert Jan |title=The Case for Auschwitz: Evidence from the Irving Trial |date=4 February 2002 |publisher=Indiana University Press |isbn=978-0-253-34016-0 |page=504 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=83dvJxPm--EC&dq=%22germar+Rudolf%22++++phd&pg=PA504 |access-date=29 October 2024 |language=en |quote=For the record: Rudolf does not hold a Ph.D.}}</ref>

Between 1991 and 1994, [[Hajo Herrmann]] and other lawyers used Rudolf's Auschwitz report to defend several Holocaust deniers. Rudolf knew his work would be associated with [[Holocaust denial]], but insisted that they had a right to legal defense. Among other things, Rudolf's report claims that only insignificant traces of cyanide compounds can be found in the samples taken from the gas chambers at Auschwitz.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Chemistry of Auschwitz |url=http://www.holocaust-history.org/auschwitz/chemistry/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080607061938/http://www.holocaust-history.org/auschwitz/chemistry/ |archive-date=7 June 2008 |access-date=7 June 2008}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Leuchter, Rudolf, and the Iron Blues |url=http://www.holocaust-history.org/auschwitz/chemistry/blue/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080616180813/http://www.holocaust-history.org/auschwitz/chemistry/blue/ |archive-date=16 June 2008 |access-date=16 June 2008}}</ref> However, [[Richard J. Green|Richard Green]] and Jamie McCarthy from [[The Holocaust History Project]], [[Robert Jan van Pelt]] from [[Holocaust Denial on Trial]], and Till Bastian in his book "''Auschwitz und die 'Auschwitz-Lüge'''" have criticized the report, saying that, among other things, like [[Fred Leuchter]] in [[Leuchter report|his report]], Rudolf did not discriminate against the formation of iron-based cyanide compounds, which are not a reliable indicator of the presence of cyanide, so that his experiment was seriously flawed.<ref name="science" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=alsalin |date=2016-05-03 |title=Appeal: Outline submissions on behalf of the First Defendant by Richard Rampton |url=https://www.hdot.org/outline/ |access-date=2025-07-25 |website=Holocaust Denial on Trial |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=kmccar6 |date=2016-09-01 |title=The Van Pelt Report by Robert Jan van Pelt |url=https://www.hdot.org/vanpelt_toc/ |access-date=2025-08-22 |website=Holocaust Denial on Trial |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Bastian |first=Till |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OiabrfihPiAC |title=Auschwitz und die "Auschwitz-Lüge": Massenmord und Geschichtsfälschung |date=1997 |publisher=C.H.Beck |isbn=978-3-406-43155-5 |language=de}}</ref>

==Criminal convictions==
In 1995, Rudolf was sentenced to 14 months in prison by the district court of [[Stuttgart]] for "inciting racial hatred" via the "Rudolf Report", as Holocaust denial is a criminal offence in Germany.<ref name="Levy2014"/>  Rudolf avoided prison by fleeing to [[Spain]], England, and finally to the [[United States]].<ref name="Atkins2009"/>  His first marriage was to a German national with whom he had two children, and they settled at [[Hastings]] in England, until he and his wife divorced and she returned to Germany with their children.<ref name=sp>[http://germarrudolf.com/a-rebel/ A Rebel] at germarrudolf.com, accessed 27 October 2015</ref>

On 11 September 2004, Rudolf married a US citizen and settled in [[Chicago]]; the couple later had a child.<ref>David Cole, ''Republican Party Animal: The "Bad Boy of Holocaust History" Blows the Lid'' (2014), p. 120</ref> He applied for [[political asylum]], or at least for the right not to be expelled, but this was rejected in November 2004 on the basis that the application had no merits and was a case of [[frivolous litigation]]. Rudolf appealed against this ruling, and in early 2006 the US Federal Court in [[Atlanta]] found that his application to stay in the country was not "frivolous", but upheld the decision that it had no merit.<ref name=scheerer>{{cite web|url=https://caselaw.findlaw.com/us-11th-circuit/1448724.html |title=Scheerer v. Chertoff DHS |author=US Court of Appeals, Eleventh District|date=15 January 2008}}</ref>  On 14 November 2005, Rudolf was deported to Germany where he was wanted for incitement of racial hatred (''[[Volksverhetzung]]'').<ref>[https://2001-2009.state.gov/g/drl/rls/hrrpt/2006/78814.htm "2006 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Germany,"] US Department of State (6 March 2007)</ref>  On arrival there, he was arrested by the police and transferred to a prison in [[Rottenburg am Neckar|Rottenburg]], then to another in [[Stuttgart]] in [[Baden-Württemberg]].{{Citation needed|date=August 2020}}

On 15 March 2007, the Mannheim District Court sentenced him to two years and six months in prison for inciting hatred, disparaging the dead, and [[libel]].<ref name="Levy2014">{{cite book |last1=Lewy |first1=Guenter |title=Outlawing Genocide Denial |date=2014 |publisher=The University of Utah Press |location=Salt Lake City |isbn= 9781607813743 |pages=33–35}}</ref> Rudolf accepted the verdict, and copies of his "Lectures on the Holocaust" were confiscated.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.n24.de/politik/article.php?articleId=107472&teaserId=108961 |title=Haft für Holocaust-Leugner |author=N24 |publisher=N24 |date=15 March 2007 |access-date=20 March 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070505013032/http://www.n24.de/politik/article.php?articleId=107472&teaserId=108961 |archive-date=5 May 2007|url-status=dead }}</ref> He was released from prison on 5 July 2009 and emigrated to the US to join his wife and daughter, acquiring a green card and obtaining permanent residence status.<ref name="york"/><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Dreisbach |first=Tom |date=2026-04-29 |title=How an antisemitic conspiracy theory made its way to a state capitol : Consider This from NPR |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/04/29/nx-s1-5803219/how-an-antisemitic-conspiracy-theory-made-its-way-to-a-state-capitol |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=NPR |language=en}}</ref>

In July 2019, Rudolf was arrested near his home in [[Red Lion, Pennsylvania|Red Lion]], Pennsylvania for "open lewdness" after being found at 4:06&nbsp;a.m. in a public park "naked from the waist down;" he asserted that he was there exercising. He was later found guilty of indecent exposure and open lewdness, for which he was sentenced to two years of probation.<ref name="york">{{cite news| url=https://www.ydr.com/story/news/2019/07/09/germar-rudolf-holocaust-denier-charged-open-lewdness-red-lion-pa/1685114001/ |publisher=[[York Daily Record]]|last=Argento|first=Mike|title=Red Lion man charged with open lewdness is an internationally known Holocaust denier|access-date=28 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Segelbaum |first=Dylan |title=Convicted Holocaust denier who was 'naked from the waist down' found guilty in York County |url=https://www.ydr.com/story/news/crime/2020/07/07/internationally-known-holocaust-denier-found-guilty-indecent-exposure-open-lewdness-york-county/5386652002/ |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=[[York Daily Record]] |language=en-US}}</ref> On August 12, 2022, he was charged with trespassing on school grounds and disorderly conduct, and two weeks later on August 26 he was charged a second time with trespassing on school grounds; he plead guilty to those charges.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=17 February 2026 |title=York County Court of Common Pleas, Court Summary -Rudolf, Germar |url=https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/28031910-germar-rudolf-court-of-common-pleas-summary/?mode=document}}</ref> He and his wife have divorced, a change that could prejudice his immigration status in the US.<ref name=":1" />

==Publications==
After Rudolf was dismissed from the Max Planck Institute, he began to publish books promoting Holocaust denial. He founded Castle Hill Publishers<ref>{{cite news|last=Kamm|first=Oliver|authorlink=Oliver Kamm|url=http://www.thejc.com/comment-and-debate/comment/126711/respectable-revisionists|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141227103635/http://www.thejc.com/comment-and-debate/comment/126711/respectable-revisionists|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 December 2014|title='Respectable' revisionists|work=The Jewish Chronicle|date=11 December 2014|access-date=24 December 2017}}</ref> in 1997<ref name="Atkins2009">{{cite book |last1=Atkins |first1=Stephen E. |author-link=Stephen E. Atkins|title=Holocaust Denial as an International Movement |date=2009 |publisher=Praeger |location=Westport, CT & London |isbn=9780313345388 |pages=112–114 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=M9Uj6u6b-ZIC&pg=PA113}}</ref> based in [[Hastings]], England with Theses & Dissertations Press as its American outlet. In 2000, Rudolf initiated an English language Holocaust Handbooks Series, a series of Holocaust denial titles which, as of 2013, encompassed 25 titles. Furthermore, Rudolf is closely associated with the Belgian Holocaust denial organization ''Vrij Historisch Onderzoek'' (VHO).<ref name="Long2002"/> He also runs the VHO's website which is interlinked with the website of [[Bradley Smith (Holocaust denier)|Bradley Smith]]'s Committee for Open Debate on the Holocaust (CODOH).<ref name="Grumke2002"/> Until his arrest in late 2005, he published the now defunct "Vierteljahreshefte für freie Geschichtsforschung" (Quarterly journal for free historical research),<ref name="Virchow2013">{{cite book |last1=Mentel |first1=Christian|last2=Virchow|first2=Fabian|title=Vierteljahreshefte für freie Geschichtsforschung (Belgien/ Großbritannien, 1997–2007). In Benz, Wolfgang, ed. Handbuch Des Antisemitismus Judenfeindschaft in Geschichte Und Gegenwart. Band 6, Publikationen |date=2013 |publisher=De Gruyter Saur |isbn= 978-3-11-030535-7 |pages=730–732}}</ref> described by the German Office for the Protection of the Constitution as "a right-wing extremist organ."<ref>[http://www.bmi.bund.de/cae/servlet/contentblob/150332/publicationFile/13493/Verfassungsschutzbericht_2002_Id_25070_de.pdf ''Annual Report of the Office for the Protection of the Constitution 2002''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726172435/http://www.bmi.bund.de/cae/servlet/contentblob/150332/publicationFile/13493/Verfassungsschutzbericht_2002_Id_25070_de.pdf |date=26 July 2011}}, Right-Wing Extremist Activities, VII. Revisionism, “German revisionist uses foreign press for agitation,” Page 84.</ref>
